verdict.rationale: Neon documents branch reset and restore as first-party operations: the MCP tool surface lists create/reset/restore branches and finalizing a branch restore from a snapshot. The docs describe restores that keep the same connection string and moving between versions instantly, and a production user independently reports periodically resetting a branch to its parent. Missing for 10: in-depth first-party documentation of reset-from-parent mechanics and point-in-time restore windows (the Instant restore page appears only as a title), and hands-on corroboration of restoring to an earlier timestamp.

support.subject: As a developer, I can reset a branch from its parent or restore it to an earlier state without rebuilding from a dump

citations.quote: create/reset/restore branches, "Finalize branch restore from snapshot"
restores them without changing the connection string, by transferring compute endpoints to a new branch via the `finalize_restore: true` flag
Restores allow platforms to move between versions instantly.
periodically reset the branch to its parent
